title: Level 1 Buffalo Chicken Wings
summary: Dry-cured, deep-fried wings tossed in a glossy homemade buffalo sauce of Frank's RedHot, Worcestershire and vinegar, thickened lightly and emulsified with cold butter.
notes: Video: 'The Best Chicken Wings At Home (3 Levels)' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe for the same video (it links this video): https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/the-best-chicken-wings-at-home-3-levels-recipe (one page for all three levels: serves 4, prep 20 min, cook 45 min). Level 1 of 3. Servings: he says 2 lb of wings is enough for about two people ('a pound per person'), and every level uses 2 lb, so we use 2 servings (stated, video); the written recipe says 4. Times are left null: the page's 20 + 45 minutes cover all three levels together and are not split by level; the cure also needs 1-2 hours, ideally overnight. The cure (salt and baking soda) stays on the wings and is counted in full. The 2 lb is the as-bought weight of whole wings with bone (and tips, which he says you may remove), entered as bought (house rule 12); the lead converts it to edible weight. Absorbed oil uses the as-bought weight. The wings are deep-fried in vegetable oil: the pot of oil is excluded and absorbed oil is added at 10% of the raw weight with any counted coating (house rule; arithmetic on that line). Sauce: the video states every amount. He says the buffalo sauce makes enough for 4 lb of wings and tosses 2 lb, so his stated share, 50% of each sauce ingredient, is counted (house rule 10; text keeps the full batch). He adds the cornstarch slurry only until the sauce thickens; we count all of it (it is 1 Tbsp). Salt in the sauce is optional and he does not add it, so it is not counted (house rule 11). Absorbed oil: 92 g. The written recipe also lists carrot and celery sticks and ranch for serving; the video does not show them for this level, so they are not included. Hot sauce uses a generic ready-to-serve hot pepper sauce record.

steps.text: If using whole wings, cut away the flap of skin at the joint, bend the joint until it pops, and cut through it to separate the drum. Do the same at the next joint to take off the tip if you like (freeze tips for stock).
Toss the drums and flats with the kosher salt and baking soda, rubbing it in well. Arrange on a wire rack over a baking sheet and refrigerate uncovered 1-2 hours, ideally overnight, to dry the skin.
Sauce: whisk the hot sauce, Worcestershire and vinegar in a small pot and bring to a light simmer over medium heat.
Stir the cornstarch and water into a smooth slurry. Whisk it into the simmering sauce a little at a time, stopping as soon as it starts to thicken, then turn off the heat.

Off the heat, whisk in the garlic, then the cold butter a few cubes at a time, letting each addition mostly melt, until the sauce is a smooth, glossy orange emulsion that coats a spoon. Add salt only if needed, and lightly.

Heat vegetable oil, half filling a 7-quart pot, to 350°F. Fry the wings in 2-3 batches, lowering them in gently away from you, about 5-8 minutes until golden, crisp and cooked through. Drain on a wire rack.
Put the hot wings in a bowl, pour the sauce around the edge and a little over the top, and toss until fully coated. Garnish and serve.
